record.original_question: If δ_n = (−1)^(n choose 2), does the identity in Conjecture 6.3(c) hold: δ_n Σ_{λ⊢n} f_λ^2 ∏_{u∈λ} c_sp(u)^2 = n! Σ_{λ⊢n} f_λ ∏_{u∈λ} c_sp(u)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.3(c) Let δ_n = (−1)^(n choose 2). Combining conjectures 6.2(c) and 6.3(b), we have the identity δ_n Σ_{λ⊢n} f_λ^2 ∏_{u∈λ} c_sp(u)^2 = n! Σ_{λ⊢n} f_λ ∏_{u∈λ} c_sp(u).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer partition λ = (λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ … ) of n (written λ ⊢ n), let λ' denote its conjugate partition and let f_λ denote the number of standard Young tableaux of shape λ. For a cell u = (i,j) of the Young diagram of λ (so 1 ≤ j ≤ λ_i), define the symplectic content of u by
  c_sp(i,j) = λ_i + λ_j − i − j + 2,  if i > j,
  c_sp(i,j) = i + j − λ'_i − λ'_j,    if i ≤ j.
Set δ_n = (−1)^{C(n,2)}, where C(n,2) = n(n−1)/2. Prove or disprove the identity
  δ_n · Σ_{λ ⊢ n} f_λ² · Π_{u ∈ λ} c_sp(u)²  =  n! · Σ_{λ ⊢ n} f_λ · Π_{u ∈ λ} c_sp(u),
for every nonnegative integer n.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 preprint titled "Hook-Lengths, Symplectic/Orthogonal Contents and Amdeberhan's Conjectures" (arXiv:2404.01973) proves a family of hook-content identities whose t = 0 specialization yields exactly this conjectured identity, thereby establishing it. The work is presented as a corollary of more general theorems on symplectic and orthogonal content generating functions.

status_evidence.title: Hook-Lengths, Symplectic/Orthogonal Contents and Amdeberhan's Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Amdeberhan proposed several conjectures about infinite product formulas for certain generating functions of hook-lengths and symplectic/orthogonal contents.
status_evidence.claim: This paper proves Amdeberhan's symplectic-content conjectures, including the identity in question, as the t=0 case of more general theorems.

status_evidence.title: Hook-Lengths, Symplectic/Orthogonal Contents and Amdeberhan's Conjectures (HTML)
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 6.3 (c) is the special case t = 0 of the above two formulas.
status_evidence.claim: The HTML version explicitly identifies the conjectured identity as a special case of the proven theorems, confirming it is solved.
